Gnosis Pay Confirms Customer Data Exposure Following Unauthorized System Access Crypto payment card provider Gnosis Pay disclosed that unauthorized access to its legacy B2C card system was detected on November 3, exposing some customer information. The company began containment within two hours, replaced compromised credentials, and addressed the vulnerability. Gnosis Pay said customer funds and its enterprise white-label card platform were unaffected. It has increased card and wallet monitoring, made 3D Secure verification mandatory for all online card payments, and notified affected customers. The legacy system is scheduled to be retired on December 20. — link

Bitcoin Core Developer Proposes Collateral and Auction Mechanisms to Deter Quantum Theft Bitcoin Core developer Cory Fields has outlined three proposed mechanisms, Quantum Landmines, Staked Auction, and Sats Auction, to deter future quantum-enabled Bitcoin theft. Under the proposed framework, spending legacy BTC after quantum attacks become feasible would require equivalent BTC collateral. Quantum Landmines would allow owners who established cryptographic proofs in advance to protect their funds and claim an attacker's collateral. The auction mechanisms would introduce financial risks for attackers even when the original private keys are believed to be lost, allowing third parties to compete for the attacker's collateral. In the proposed Staked Auction design, the vulnerable BTC would be burned rather than recovered by its original owner. Fields emphasized that the mechanisms remain conceptual, with implementation details yet to be developed. — link

Aave Labs Acquires Avon Team and Technology to Expand Fixed-Rate Lending Aave Labs, the core developer behind DeFi lending protocol Aave, has acquired Avon's team and technology to expand into fixed-rate lending. The deal includes Avon's fixed- and floating-rate lending protocols, onchain order book, domains, and related assets. Financial terms were not disclosed. Three Avon team members will join Aave Labs, including two engineers and one business development associate. CEO Stani Kulechov said fixed-rate products could help Aave reach institutions, fintech firms, and retail users. Aave currently has over $30 billion in deposits and more than $12 billion in active loans. — link

US Treasury Moves to Cut MEXC Global Off From US Financial System Over $16B in Illicit Transactions The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has issued an order prohibiting US financial institutions from processing funds transfers to or from crypto exchange MEXC Global. FinCEN said MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and other illicit activities between May 2021 and May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and approximately $1 billion in direct transactions with Iranian crypto exchanges. FinCEN cited severe deficiencies in MEXC's anti-money laundering controls. The order will take effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. — link
